bibliographic_scope.title: Synthesis of Tungsten Carbide Nanocrystal via a Simple Reductive Reaction
bibliographic_scope.authors: Chunli Guo; Yi Liu; Xiaojian Ma; Yitai Qian; Liqiang Xu

source_interpretation.text: The authors propose that Mg reduces WO3 and ethanol to reactive W and C, followed by carbide formation. Equations describe a proposed mechanism; intermediate yields were not measured.

evidence.locator: Main PDF p. 1–2, Equations 1–7 and mechanism discussion

source_interpretation.text: Higher ethanol filling correlates with fewer other tungsten phases in the source XRD series. The paper attributes this to system pressure without giving pressure measurements.

evidence.locator: Main PDF p. 1–2, Filling discussion and Figure 2

source_interpretation.text: Excess carbon is proposed to deposit on WC surfaces. Both carbon-coated and carbon-free particles are observed; no uniform coating or population fraction is claimed.

evidence.locator: Main PDF p. 2, Figure 3 and mechanism discussion

characterization.xrd: Rigaku D/max-rA; graphite-monochromatized Cu Kα, wavelength 1.5418 Å.
characterization.microscopy: JEM2100 TEM/HRTEM; Figure 3c randomly selected particle SAED contains carbon and WC spots.
characterization.reference_cell: JCPDS 51-0939: a=2.906 Å, c=2.837 Å; reference values, not the source-refined cell. Carbon (002) reference JCPDS 26-1077.

evidence.locator: Main PDF p. 1–2, Characterization, Figure 1 and Figure 3

prior_literature_context.scope: Introduction only; cited full sources unreviewed and no recipes or outcomes imported.
prior_literature_context.method_temperatures: Direct carbonization 1400–1600 °C; ball milling and solid-state metathesis 1000 °C; metal-complex pyrolysis 700 °C; plasma-enhanced chemical vapor deposition 850 °C; sol–gel 900 °C; cited W/Na/dry-ice route 600 °C.
prior_literature_context.applications: Hardness, wear resistance, catalysis and fuel-cell motivation are cited background, not measured source properties.

limitations: Complete supplied two-page main, Figures 1–3, equations 1–7 and all 16 references. SI and cited full sources unreviewed.

The typical synthesis is quantified, but autoclave liner, internal pressure, gas handling, cooling duration, acid concentration/volume/contact time, wash volumes/counts, vacuum level and product yield are unreported.

The 30%, 50%, 75% and 90% ethanol filling series has source-linked XRD outcomes, but independent charge masses, reaction schedules and workups are not restated per specimen. Do not inherit the typical 12 mL charge or 15 h duration as a separately verified filling-series protocol.
Short-time, low-temperature and precursor-substitution controls do not have exact sample conditions or quantitative outcomes. They remain supporting observations, not additional complete recipes.

The source describes both carbon-coated and carbon-free WC populations without separate preparation or batch labels. No coating thickness, population fractions or measured atomic/particle coordinates are supplied.
The source proposes a pressure effect from ethanol filling; no absolute pressure was measured/reported. Mechanistic equations are authors’ proposals, not measured intermediate yields.
No electrical, catalytic, hardness or other application property was measured in this paper; introductory application claims remain literature context.
Independent source comparison passed; molecular/particle/reference-cell presentation remains pending.
